title: HomeFlood Underwriting Rule: One Live Policy per Address, NFIP Overlap and the Package Credit
content:
## 1. One live policy per address

Only one HomeFlood Private Residential Flood Policies policy may be live on a property address. A new HomeFlood policy is issued only when no other HomeFlood policy at the same property address is pending effective, active or pending cancellation. This is decided from Tidemark's own policy records for that address, not from the customer's account of them.

| Status of another HomeFlood policy at the same address | New HomeFlood policy at that address |
|---|---|
| pending effective | not issued |
| active | not issued |
| pending cancellation | not issued |

## 2. No HomeFlood over a live Tidemark NFIP building policy

Tidemark does not write HomeFlood over its own live NFIP Dwelling Form building policy on the same building. When the customer holds a Dwelling Form policy with building coverage at the same property address, and that policy is pending effective, in force or in renewal grace, HomeFlood can be issued only on these terms:

- the waiting-period basis is NFIP replacement;
- the effective date equals the date on which the NFIP policy's cancellation, for the reason replaced by private flood, takes effect;
- the NFIP policy number is recorded as the replaced NFIP policy number.

## 3. Package credit

Holding a Tidemark Excess Flood policy in status active at the same property address on the term start earns the package credit for that term; the credit is decided at issue and at each renewal and is not added or removed mid-term.

*Status of clause 3:* as the basis for the re-rated term premium worked out when an Elevation Certificate review is completed, this clause is **no longer in force**. For every other HomeFlood rating it continues to apply as written above.

The package credit rests on an Excess Flood policy, status active, at the same property address, on the term start.

*Hypothetical illustration:* an Excess Flood policy at the address becomes active one week after a HomeFlood term starts. It earns nothing for that term, because the credit is fixed at issue or renewal and is not added mid-term; it is considered again at the next renewal.
